To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the uORFs of the AtHB1 gene and its homolog in maize are conserved and that the uORFS repress the translation of the AtHBI and its maize homologs in aerial tissues that were exposed to light.
the expression of the transcription factor AtHB1 is repressed posttranscriptionally by the uORF CPuORF, which causes ribosome staling in aerial tissues that were exposed to light.

an uORF located in the 5′-UTR of a gene for a homeodomain-leu-zine transcription factor causes ribosome stall in aerial tissues exposed to light, which results in the repression of the main open read-ing frame and, ultimately, in a deleterious phenotype for the plant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a uORF that represses the expression of a transcription factor that is required for plant development.

the regulation of a transcription factor by a uORF, which causes ribosome stall in aerial tissues that have been exposed to light, and with the role of the CPuORFs in the control of the plant phenotype.
the identification of a novel uORF that is involved in plant development and whose regulation is mediated by a chloroplast-derived signal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a uORF in the 5′ untranslated sequence of a homeodomain-leu-zine transcription factor gene causes ribosome stailing, and this is a mechanism to prevent a deleterious phenotype.
the AtHB1 uORF is a regulatory element that represses the translation of the AtHB1 mRNA in aerial tissues exposed to light.

the uORFs in the AtHB1 and ZmHb1 transcripts are involved in the translational regulation of the homeodomain-leu-zine zipper I transcription factors in aerial tissues, and this regulation is mediated by a light-dependent signal from the chloroplast.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CPuORFs, which are present in the 5′ untranslated regions of many genes, are a new class of regulatory elements whose function is tissue specific and depends on the light conditions.
a uORF encoded in a homeodomain-leukine zipper transcription factor gene causes ribosome staling and represses its translation in aerial tissues exposed to light.
the CPuORFs are a new class of regulatory peptides that are conserved in the angiosperm kingdom and that repress the expression of a subset of homeodomain-leu-cine zipper I genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
uORF-mediated ribosome stalling can be used as a regulatory mechanism to repress the expression of transcription factors in aerial tissues that have been exposed to light.
the uORFs in the 5′ untranslated regions of homeodomain-leukine zipper transcription factor genes are a conserved mechanism to avoid a deleterious effect of these proteins.
the presence of a uORF is not necessarily deleterious for a gene and that it may be used to fine-tune gene expression in a tissue-specific and developmental stage–dependent manner.
